title: `go generate`: code generation as part of the build

videos.script: Some Go code is not written by a person. A program writes it, and the go command runs that program when you ask. This lesson is about that step, go generate. {{directive}} It starts with a comment. A line that begins with slash slash go colon generate names a command. Go generate finds those lines and runs them, one at a time, in the package's own directory. Go build never runs them. That one fact shapes the rest of the lesson. {{stringer}} Then the generator Go's own source uses most, stringer. Five constants for the classes of HTTP status go in. A String method comes out, with a guard that breaks the build if the constants change. {{own}} Next, a generator of your own. A text file that another team keeps becomes a Go map, laid out the way gofmt would lay it out. A mistake in the file stops the generator, and it names the line. {{honest}} Last, keeping it honest. Generated files are committed. A header line tells tools to leave them alone. And a check in continuous integration generates everything again, and fails when anything moved. By the end, hits carries generated code, and you can trust it.
